issues.description: The problem instructions explicitly require students to output the columns ID, Name, Art and URL and additionally state 'benenne keine ... Spalten mit AS, wenn du nicht dazu aufgefordert wirst.' However the provided solution (aufgabe01.sql) aliases the name column as id (SELECT name as id, name, art, url), producing a duplicated name column and using an alias instead of an actual ID column. This contradicts the problem guidance and may confuse students about whether they must use a real ID column or are allowed/expected to alias another column to 'id'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem instructions by selecting the actual ID column from the Schwimmbad table (e.g. SELECT id, name, art, url ...) rather than aliasing name as id, or alternatively update the problem text to explicitly allow aliasing and explain why name may be used as the ID if the table lacks a dedicated id column. Also remove the unnecessary duplicate name column produced by the alias.

issues.description: The problem statement asks for an output containing an "ID" column for Freibäder, but the solution aliases the "name" column as id (SELECT name as id, ...). This creates a naming mismatch: students may expect a real primary key column named id in the Schwimmbad table (and the template SELECT * would include it if present), yet the solution repurposes the name column as 'id'. This inconsistency can confuse students about which column is the actual identifier and whether they should reference an existing 'id' column or alias another field.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier naming consistent: either (A) update the solution to select the actual id column from Schwimmbad (e.g. SELECT id, name, art, url ...) if such a column exists, or (B) update the problem statement to explicitly state that the 'Name' should be used/aliased as 'ID' if no id column exists. Ensure the template, problem text, and solution all reference the same column name for the identifier.
